mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.2% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, as investors anticipate future rate hikes, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.22 in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns during inflation spikes are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not revert to baseline within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.3% signals wage pressures that prompt equity market anticipation of higher earnings, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 0.3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes with rising unemployment, the 60-day forward return correlation with PAYEMS acceleration is below 0.2 in absolute value, or IC < 0.05 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in RSAFS retail sales of more than 2% indicates weakening consumer demand, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 30 such contraction episodes, less than 10% of predicted negative returns materialize, or RSAFS recovers within 2 weeks with SPX returns also positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in INDPRO manufacturing index below 95 signals supply-side softness that reduces market optimism, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 95 in the current month
failure_condition: During confirmed supply shocks, the 20-day forward return is positive in >50% of INDPRO < 95 events (t-test p < 0.05), or IC > 0.1 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in FEDFUNDS rates for three consecutive months creates a forward discounting effect, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days when the decline is persistent (>0.25% monthly).
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls by >0.25% each month for three months
failure_condition: During such cycles, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than average (t-test p > 0.05), or the effect disappears after 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months amid rising employment (PAYEMS > 143000), it indicates a softening labor market that increases equity risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND PAYEMS > 143000 in the current month
failure_condition: In this regime, the 20-day forward return is negative in >70% of such events (IC < -0.15), or the correlation with labor cost growth is negative (> -0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time drop in HOUST housing starts exceeding -5% in a month is interpreted as a housing soft landing signal, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST drops by more than 5% in a single month
failure_condition: Over 10 such events, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05), or HOUST recovers within 2 days with no SPX response.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO falls by more than 8% in a month and RSAFS also declines by >10%, it signals simultaneous supply-side shocks that produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO down >8% AND RSAFS down >10% in the current month
failure_condition: During such co-movements, the 20-day forward return is positive in >50% of cases (IC > 0.1), or the effect is not significant after controlling for inflation and interest rates (F-test p > 0.05).
